text.brief: A budget analyst at the Pentagon compares two lines in 2031. The shield's space layer has doubled in cost, and the Navy's munitions account for the Pacific falls short of the same sum.
text.record: The President ordered a missile shield for the homeland in January 2025, and its program lead later put the cost at about $185 billion ([Executive Order 14186, The Iron Dome for America](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/02/03/2025-02182/the-iron-dome-for-america)). The Congressional Budget Office estimated in May 2026 that a system meeting the order could cost $1.2 trillion over 20 years, most of it for about 7,800 interceptors in orbit. The Pentagon reported in December 2025 that the mainland's stockpile stood in the low 600s and would exceed 1,000 by 2030.
text.reading: The Party lures America onto ground where each interceptor costs more than the missile it chases. Every American layer justifies another Party silo, and every dollar spent in orbit leaves the Pacific short of ships and munitions. This is Stratagem 15, lure the tiger down the mountain.
text.coreEvent: The Pentagon estimates the mainland's operational nuclear warheads at more than 1,000 before 2032.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. No cost-exchange test governs how much of the budget each layer may take.
text.fix: Fund each layer only when it passes a cost-exchange test against the threat it must stop.
